LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD for the GoLand JetBrains IDE is safe to source for `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. At the top/global scope, only standard variable and array assignments occur: `pkgbase`, `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `options`, `source`, and `b2sums`. There are no command substitutions, no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget` invocations, no encoded blobs, and no data exfiltration paths at parse time.

The `source` array references `https://download.jetbrains.com/go/${pkgbase}-${pkgver}.tar.gz`, which is JetBrains' official download host for GoLand -- an expected upstream source for this package. Checksums are provided via `b2sums` (not SKIP). The two function bodies (`package_goland()` and `package_goland-jre()`) are not executed at the printsrcinfo stage; they only contain standard file installation operations (cp, install, rm, ln) into `$pkgdir`, which is normal packaging behavior and out of scope for this gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard JetBrains GoLand PKGBUILD, no top-level execution risk.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard `.nvchecker.toml` configuration file used by the AUR packaging infrastructure. The file configures nvchecker (a version checking tool) to monitor JetBrains' official data services API for new GoLand releases. The URL `https://data.services.jetbrains.com/products?code=GO&release.type=release` is the legitimate upstream endpoint for checking GoLand release information. The regex pattern simply extracts version numbers from the response. There are no suspicious network requests to untrusted hosts, no obfuscation, no data exfiltration, and no unexpected file operations. This is routine packaging tooling for tracking upstream updates.
</details>
